target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter surviving-value consumer (native entry 29)
target.role: pop one value and pass it to a call, with a global field as the other argument
target.notes: native dispatch entry 29, code address 0x080007E6, 24 bytes and 11 instructions, one terminator at 0x080007FC. A mechanical scan of both proven dispatch tables found 52 functions that pop a stack value and do NOT write a result back into the slot; this is the smallest of them, with one pop, one call, one literal and no branches. It is the first routine in the target chain that turns a surviving stack value into an actual use: it decrements the counter, reads values[count-1], and passes that value as the SECOND argument (r1) to sub_08004380, with the FIRST argument (r0) being the +0x14 field of the object at the routine's only literal 0x08054FBC. Nothing is written back to the stack, so the consumed slot keeps its old value and no result replaces it, which is what distinguishes it from the arithmetic family. Ordering is proven by the self-check reading the counter from inside the callee: the counter store precedes the value read, which precedes the call. UNDERFLOW IS HARMLESS TO MEMORY here, unlike the arithmetic family: a zero counter becomes 0xFFFFFFFF, the base becomes context-4, and [slot+4] is therefore context itself, so the value passed on underflow is the brand-new counter 0xFFFFFFFF; because the routine has no store to the slot, nothing below the context is read or written. A second underflow walks the base down and reads pre[3] instead. No guard was added. The callee is declared, not reconstructed, and no meaning is imported from another title.

verdicts_are_independent: SEMANTIC, MODERN_BUILD and ADS_MATCH answer different questions and none is evidence for another. A passing modern build says nothing about the original compiler; a passing semantic run only removes one class of error.

identity.why_not: the original translation unit was built by ARM Developer Suite 1.2 (the surviving command line names tcpp). GCC is a different compiler with a different code generator, so its output cannot establish anything about ADS 1.2.

literal_pools.interpretation: the original's literals are accounted for by the words the unit declares; the modern build pools differently, which is a structural consequence of the compiler rather than a defect in the reconstruction. It is also why a function with a literal load cannot be compared standalone.

comparison.match_claim_note: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This compares a modern GCC build against the cartridge. A modern compiler is not the original compiler, so a difference here is expected and proves nothing; an identity here would also prove nothing about ADS 1.2. ADS_MATCH stays BLOCKED.
